newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi border quiet, no sign of Turk troops -- UN.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi border quiet, no sign of Turk troops -- UN.

text.p: United Nations officials and Kurdish guerrilla forces said on Friday the border with Turkey was quiet, with no evidence that Turkish troops or aircraft had struck at Kurdish separatist camps inside northern Iraq.
"All we have heard are rumours and news reports. We have not sighted any Turkish troops on the ground and we have seen no airplanes," said a U.N. official in this border town.

"We have not spoken with an NGO (non-governmental organisation) who has seen that either. If they were there, I think we would know it," said the U.N. official, in radio contact with monitors and aide groups around the area.

The U.N. official was reinforcing foreign ministry and military statements in Ankara on Thursday that Turkish forces had not gone into action against Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels, based just inside Iraq.
Border forces of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), which generally control the Iraqi side, confirmed the U.N. account.

On Thursday, Turkish toops and equipment were seen moving near the border, apparently part of preparations to set up a security zone in Iraq. Washington has said it would not object as long as the operation were short-lived.
